title: ci(lint): every job in lint.yml carries a `timeout-minutes` derived from its measured duration — `Lint & Repo Gates` has none, so a hang holds the merge-queue head until GitHub's 360-minute default
body:
Path: devpath · CI gates · the `Lint & Type Check` workflow (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`)
Unblocks: the merge queue for every PR on this repository (a hang in the queue head's `Lint & Repo Gates` holds every entry behind it)

**Maintainer's direct order** (live director chat, 2026-10-01 ~03:3x UTC, verbatim): 「Lint & Repo Gates 这个 job 没有 timeout-minutes ，这个问题你负责派发解决。」 Filed and dispatched by the director seat (summon #31, `session_01PGMD6TRDaZY8Ubyo7Ukm66`) under that order. `tooling` + `domain:spec` (`.github/workflows/` wiring anchors to the spec lane per the lane table).

## The defect

`.github/workflows/lint.yml` declares six jobs. Five carry no `timeout-minutes` (read at `origin/main` `2a4254a608`):

| job id | `name:` (the check context) | `timeout-minutes` | measured p50 / p99 / max (minutes) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `lint` | `Lint & Repo Gates` (**required**, ruleset 12119582) | none → GitHub default 360 | 15.8 / 32.6 / 32.7 (n = 81) |
| `typecheck-workspace` | `Type Check · workspace` | none | 13.0 / 16.0 / 16.0 (n = 86) |
| `typecheck-consumers` | `Type Check · consumer gates` | none | 7.7 / 10.1 / 10.1 (n = 87) |
| `typecheck-debt` | `Type Check · debt ledger` | none | 5.8 / 7.4 / 7.5 (n = 92) |
| `typecheck-source-gates` | `Type Check · source gates` | none | 3.2 / 3.5 / 3.7 (n = 94) |
| `typecheck` | `TypeScript Type Check` (**required**) | 10 | 0.1 / 0.1 / 0.2 (n = 85) |

Measurement: the 100 most recent completed runs of `lint.yml` (events `pull_request`, `merge_group`, `push`, `schedule`; window 2026-10-01T00:23Z → 03:24Z; 96 runs with jobs read, 525 successful job rows), job `started_at` → `completed_at` from the jobs API. `Lint & Repo Gates` by event: `merge_group` n = 30 p50 15.8 max 32.6; `pull_request` n = 47 p50 15.7 max 32.7; `schedule` n = 3 max 31.3. A docs-only PR (12 skipped steps) runs it in 7–11 minutes; a code PR in 25–33.

**Why it matters today, measured.** On 2026-10-01 a `Test Core (1/6)` shard went silent mid-build on the queue head (PR #20992, run 36803445860): it sat `in_progress` until its 45-minute job timeout cancelled it at 02:51:33Z, the queue removed the entry at 02:52:05Z and rebuilt every entry behind it; `main` saw no merge between 02:09:45Z and 03:19:43Z. That shard had a wall. `Lint & Repo Gates` is the longest required job in every queue group and has none: the same silence in one of its 198 sequential steps holds the queue head for GitHub's 360-minute default. The merge-queue ruleset (`check_response_timeout_minutes: 60`) would drop the entry after 60 minutes with no red check and no `Merge Queue Triage` comment (that workflow fires on `failure` only; a silent removal is neither), while the hung job keeps burning a runner for up to six hours.

## Governing text

- `AGENTS.md` → Route & surface ownership, rule 3 「Absence must be loud」: "a verifier that silently degrades … is worse than no verifier, because it reports success. Prefer failing to falling back." A job that sits `in_progress` for six hours after it stopped producing output is the silent form.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, the `Stall-guard budget invariant` step's comment (in the `lint` job): the guard's guarantee is "a stalled job says so instead of sitting in_progress until the job timeout". The lint-workflow jobs wrap no step in the stall guard (`git grep -c 'run-with-stall-guard' -- .github/workflows/lint.yml` → 0), so for these jobs the job timeout is the only wall there is.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `Test Core (${{ matrix.shard }}/6)` job: `timeout-minutes: 45` — the sibling workflow's precedent, and the wall that bounded today's stall.
- Ruleset 12119582 (`GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/rulesets/12119582`): `merge_queue.check_response_timeout_minutes: 60`, `required_status_checks` contexts include `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check`.

## Acceptance

1. Every job in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` declares `timeout-minutes`. The values, derived from the table above and ruled by the director (batch #259 rider, maintainer order): `lint` **60** (max 32.7 × ~1.8, and equal to the merge queue's 60-minute check-response window so the job turns red with GitHub's "exceeded the maximum execution time" annotation at the same moment the queue would otherwise drop the entry silently); `typecheck-workspace` **30**; `typecheck-consumers` **20**; `typecheck-debt` **15**; `typecheck-source-gates` **10**; `typecheck` stays **10**. Rule applied: about 2× the measured maximum, rounded to a 5-minute grain, never below the maximum plus 10 minutes, never above 60.
2. Each new `timeout-minutes` line carries a one-paragraph comment in the workflow stating the measured p50 / p99 / max and the window they were read over, and the rule above — so the next author re-measures instead of re-deriving; no tracker number in the comment (`pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint`-class rules), the lesson in the text.
3. The six `name:` contexts are byte-identical before and after (`scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` pins them; the required-status-check registry and the ruleset are not touched). No step is added, removed or reordered; no `concurrency:` block changes.
4. Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` run from the worktree with no paths (the change set derived from git), every command run with its exit code captured and `--ran` reconciled; `pnpm check:stall-guard-budget` (reads `.github/workflows/**`, must stay green or REFUSE for the unchanged reason, never red because of this diff); `node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs`; `actionlint` if present in the toolchain, else `node -e` YAML parse of the file.
5. PR: `Fixes` this card; draft; `skip-changeset` applies (no package publishes from `.github/workflows/`; the seat applies the label); `Clause-②: no`.

## Not in scope

- The merge-queue ruleset values (`check_response_timeout_minutes`, `max_entries_to_build`) — repository settings, the maintainer's hand.
- `Merge Queue Triage` firing on `cancelled` — a separate finding if wanted; this card makes the lint timeout fire visibly as a red check, which is enough for a human to see.
- Shortening the 198-step `Lint & Repo Gates` job (sharding, parallelism) — throughput work, its own card.

Dedupe words: lint.yml timeout-minutes, Lint & Repo Gates job timeout, merge queue head hang 360 minutes, lint workflow job wall
